newsitem.title: USA: GM wants fewer car models, more trucks.
newsitem.headline: GM wants fewer car models, more trucks.

text.p: General Motors Corp marketing chief Ronald Zarrella on Friday said he wanted the automaker to cut the number of cars it offered and expand its lineup of trucks and "crossover" vehicles.
Zarrella told reporters at the Chicago Auto Show that the company -- which offered about 82 different models in North America last year -- planned to reduce that number by an unspecified amount.
"We know we've got too many car models and not enough trucks and crossover models," he said.
Zarrella said GM's increased production of trucks and new car model introductions should allow the company to expand its market share during 1997.
"We will regain the market share we lost in 1996, if not more," he said.

GM's share of the U.S. car and truck market dipped to 31 percent in 1996 from 32.4 percent the previous year as strikes and new models took a toll on production. In January, GM's share hovered at about 30 percent.
